I will keep my full 12 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that matches my land, my irrigation condition, and the way my family can manage labor. I have only farmed for 5 years, so I will not do anything too risky. I will use better seed for both crops to keep yield stable, and I will manage fertilizer at a moderate level instead of pushing too hard, because I want dependable production more than gambling on very high output. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key stages rather than too many times, so I can control cost and still protect yield. For wheat, I will focus on steady fertilization, a few irrigations, and limited pesticide sprays because wheat needs good establishment and spring growth. After wheat harvest, I will plant maize quickly on the same 12 mu, use hybrid seed, simplify tillage with rotary work, and rely on fewer irrigations because summer rain can help, while still giving enough fertilizer for grain formation. I will keep pesticide use moderate on both crops because I want to avoid losing yield to common pests and diseases, but I also do not want unnecessary spending.
